families.label: Metric gradient flow → dissipation → exponential decay
families.plain_language: The state space changes, but the same proof skeleton can survive: choose an energy and a metric, identify its metric gradient, write energy dissipation, then use a PL-shaped inequality to turn dissipation into exponential convergence.
reading_order: metric chooses the gradient
gradient flow gives an energy-dissipation identity
metric PL closes the scalar differential inequality
only then specialize to Euclidean, Riemannian, or Wasserstein geometry
families.do_not_conflate: Wasserstein/Otto calculus needs rigorous first-variation and flow hypotheses; W2 is not globally a classical smooth finite-dimensional Riemannian manifold.

families.label: Second-order curvature → first-order/growth controls
families.plain_language: Strong convexity is not merely a faster convergence assumption. It is a lower-curvature statement that produces a quadratic lower model and, after the right geometry is chosen, often yields growth or PL-like coercivity.
reading_order: Euclidean strong-convex quadratic model
geodesic/Riemannian curvature adapter
Wasserstein geodesic convexity or Bakry-Emery curvature in their own settings
derive only the coercivity statement justified by that setting
families.do_not_conflate: Euclidean Hessian bounds, geodesic convexity, displacement convexity, and Bakry-Emery curvature are related patterns but not interchangeable hypotheses.

families.label: PL / LSI mirror: objective gap versus gradient dissipation
families.plain_language: Optimization PL bounds the objective gap by a squared gradient. For Langevin, LSI bounds KL by relative Fisher information, which is the squared Wasserstein gradient norm of KL in the smooth formal picture. Both turn the same dissipation identity into exponential gap decay.
reading_order: identify the gap functional
identify its exact dissipation / metric-gradient norm
state the PL-shaped coercivity with source normalization
apply Gronwall
families.do_not_conflate: LSI is a functional inequality for measures/densities, not literally the Euclidean PL theorem; constants and factors of two depend on normalization.

families.label: Poincare / chi-square mirror: quadratic gap versus Dirichlet dissipation
families.plain_language: For density ratio rho, chi-square is the squared L2 distance of rho from 1. Poincare controls this quadratic gap by Dirichlet energy, and reversible semigroup dissipation then gives exponential chi-square decay.
reading_order: chi-square as an L2 density gap
Poincare as coercivity of the Dirichlet form
semigroup dissipation
exponential chi-square decay
families.do_not_conflate: Poincare/chi-square and LSI/KL are parallel dissipation templates but different inequalities and generally different strengths.

families.label: Quadratic regularization: proximal minimizer or Gibbs draw
families.plain_language: Optimization and sampling can consume the same regularized energy differently: one chooses its minimizer, the other samples from its normalized exponential.
reading_order: common regularized energy
deterministic minimizer branch
Gibbs/RGO branch
separate existence, normalization, and invariance obligations
families.do_not_conflate: Sharing an energy does not make the proximal map and restricted Gaussian oracle equivalent outputs.
